title: Upper Deck Floor Beam Web — Crack Arrest and Angle Reinforcement Repair
abstract: Permanent repair for a crack in the upper deck floor beam web at a lightening hole, using a stop drill, a machined angle across the hole and a gusset at the nearest shear tie position.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the shear capability of an upper deck floor beam web after a crack has been found at a lightening hole, and arrests the crack so that it cannot grow into the beam cap.
sections.damage_assessment: Find both crack tips by dye penetrant inspection before any material is removed, and mark them. Measure the crack length along its path, not end to end. A crack that stays inside the allowable limits below may be stop drilled and left under repeat inspection. A crack that has reached a beam cap, that crosses more than one lightening hole, or that lies in the beam bay immediately under a galley monument hardpoint, is outside the scope of this repair and requires an engineering assessment. Record the beam station and the hole number before you start.
sections.repair_procedure: Stop drill both crack tips with the guided drill, taking the hole 3 mm beyond the marked tip, and ream to the finished size. Do a dye penetrant inspection of each stop drilled hole to confirm that the tip has been removed. Where the tip has not been removed, drill 3 mm further and repeat. Deburr both faces of the web. Cut the reinforcement angle D5170114531196 to the length on the repair drawing and offer it across the lightening hole so that it lands on sound material each side. Drill the fastener pattern using the angle as a template, keeping the edge distance given on the drawing and staying clear of the existing shear tie fasteners. Add the gusset UM400039-50 at the nearest shear tie position, picking up the existing fastener line where the drawing allows it. Deburr, apply the surface protection of the standard practice, and install both items wet with sealant using rivets AGS611113-6C and anchor nuts AES626292-95 at the blind positions. Restore the corrosion protection over the whole repaired area and record the fastener count.
sections.inspection_requirements: The repair has no life limit provided the crack tips were fully removed and confirmed by dye penetrant inspection. Do a repeat detailed visual inspection of the stop drilled holes and of the angle perimeter every 4 000 flight cycles. A new indication at either stop drilled hole invalidates the repair and requires an engineering assessment. The repair may not be applied twice in the same beam bay.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 30 mm along their path, starting at a lightening hole edge, not reaching a beam cap and not crossing a second hole. One crack per beam bay.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single row of 24 rivets AGS611113-6C each side of the hole at 18 mm pitch and 12 mm edge distance, with anchor nuts AES626292-95 at the four blind positions
type_data.fatigue_life_note: No life limit when both crack tips are confirmed removed. Repeat detailed visual inspection every 4 000 flight cycles.
